test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a discretionary power of the President of India?

options.text: Dissolving the Lok Sabha without advice
Appointing the Chief Justice of India
Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority
Giving assent to a Money Bill

solution:
The correct answer is __**Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Discretionary powers of the President of India:** The President of India holds discretionary powers, which are exercised only under certain circumstances. These powers allow the President to act without the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• When no political party secures a clear majority in the Lok Sabha, the President has the authority to use his/her discretion in appointing the Prime Minister. *Hence, appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority is a discretionary power.*
 
• The President may invite the leader of the largest party or coalition to form the government, provided they can prove majority support in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Other situations where the President exercises discretionary powers include dismissing a government when it loses majority and recommending the dissolution of Lok Sabha if no viable government can be formed.
 
• The President does not have the discretion to dissolve the Lok Sabha without the advice of the Council of Ministers. This is governed by Article 85 of the Constitution. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Appointing the Chief Justice of India is not a discretionary power. The President appoints the Chief Justice based on established conventions and recommendations from the judiciary. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Giving assent to a Money Bill is not a discretionary power of the President. Under Article 110, the President can only approve or reject a Money Bill but cannot return it for reconsideration. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Discretionary Powers of the President:**

 
 
• Discretionary powers are exercised by the President in situations where the advice of the Council of Ministers is not available or applicable.
 
• Examples include appointing the Prime Minister when no party secures a majority in the Lok Sabha or dissolving the Lok Sabha when no viable government can be formed.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Prime Minister:**
 
 
• When no single party achieves a majority, the President invites the leader of the largest coalition or party to form the government.
 
• The appointed Prime Minister must prove majority support in the Lok Sabha within a stipulated time frame.
 
• **Example:** In 1989, when no party achieved a majority, then President **R. Venkataraman** appointed **V. P. Singh** as Prime Minister after consultation with various leaders.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• **Article 75:** It states that the President appoints the Prime Minister and other members of the Council of Ministers.
 
• **Article 85:** The President summons, prorogues, and dissolves the Lok Sabha based on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President’s discretionary powers are used in exceptional circumstances, ensuring the democratic process is upheld.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Discretionary Powers:**

 
 
• The discretionary powers of the President are limited and are exercised only in rare situations like a hung parliament or no clear majority.
 
• These powers are intended to maintain the smooth functioning of parliamentary democracy and ensure governance continuity.
 
 
 
• **Historical Examples:**
 
 
• **1996:** After the general elections, then-President **Shankar Dayal Sharma** appointed **A. B. Vajpayee** as Prime Minister for 13 days when BJP emerged as the single largest party but failed to prove majority.
 
• **1989:** When Congress lost the majority, President **R. Venkataraman** appointed **V. P. Singh** as Prime Minister, who later proved his majority in the Lok Sabha.
